response.sql:
WITH large AS (
  SELECT MediaTypeId, Bytes, Milliseconds
  FROM Track
  WHERE Bytes > 10323804
),
per_type AS (
  SELECT MediaTypeId,
         AVG(Bytes * 1.0 / NULLIF(Milliseconds, 0)) AS avg_bytes_per_ms,
         COUNT(*) AS track_count
  FROM large
  GROUP BY MediaTypeId
)
SELECT AVG(avg_bytes_per_ms) AS avg_of_avg_bytes_per_ms,
       AVG(track_count) AS avg_track_count
FROM per_type;

assumptions.assumption: "Large" means Bytes strictly greater than 10,323,804; NULL Bytes are excluded by the comparison.
Rows with Milliseconds = 0 are treated as missing (NULLIF yields NULL, so they drop out of the per-type average). Track counts include every large track in the group.
The SQL targets SQLite, which the backtick-quoted schema suggests; the query also runs on PostgreSQL and MySQL with minor changes.

alternatives.interpretation: "Large" includes tracks whose Bytes equals the cutoff exactly (at least 10,323,804 bytes).
